about: A synthetic syllabus. Invented for this module: the sessions, the concepts and the notes are made up, and none of it describes a real course, a real person or a real event.

sessions.title: Two ways to find a passage

concepts.name: Tokens and the context window
concepts.note: A model reads tokens, not characters and not words. The context window is how many tokens one call can hold, and everything competes for it: the system prompt, the retrieved passages, the conversation so far. When the window fills, something is dropped, and nothing tells you what was dropped.

concepts.name: Prompt shape
concepts.note: A prompt is a contract written in prose. Put the task first, the constraints next, and the material last, so the model reads the instructions before the thing it has to act on. A vague prompt fails quietly: you get an answer, and the answer is plausible.

concepts.name: Structured output
concepts.note: Ask for JSON, then validate it. A response that parses is not the same as a response that is correct, so the schema lists the fields you will actually read and rejects the ones you will not. An unknown field fails validation, because a contract that accepts anything is not a contract.

concepts.name: Chunking
concepts.note: Split a document into passages small enough to retrieve and large enough to mean something. Prefer paragraph boundaries over a fixed character count: a chunk that ends mid-sentence retrieves badly and reads worse. Overlap costs storage and buys you the sentence that straddles a boundary.

concepts.name: Lexical search
concepts.note: Score a passage by how many query words it shares, weighted so that common words count for less. It is cheap, it is inspectable, and it has one hard limit: it matches a fixed vocabulary, so a question worded differently from the document scores zero.

concepts.name: Embeddings
concepts.note: An embedding turns a passage into a vector, so that two ways of saying the same thing land near each other. The gain is paraphrase. The cost is that you cannot read a vector and say why two passages matched.

concepts.name: Retrieval
concepts.note: Retrieval decides what the model sees. Order the candidates, cut the list, pass the top few: ranking badly and then passing everything is the same as not retrieving at all. Combine word scores and vector scores when neither alone covers the questions you actually get.

concepts.name: Grounding and citations
concepts.note: An answer is grounded when every claim in it traces to a passage that was retrieved. Citations that point nowhere are worse than no citations: they look like evidence and they are decoration. When nothing was retrieved, refuse.

concepts.name: Cost tracking
concepts.note: Count tokens per call and per answer, and record the count beside the answer. A cost surprise is almost never one expensive call. It is a cheap call inside a loop that nobody counted.

concepts.name: Tool calling
concepts.note: A tool is a function the model may ask you to run. Validate the arguments before running anything, because the arguments are model output, and model output is untrusted input.

concepts.name: The agent loop
concepts.note: The loop is: decide, call a tool, read the result, repeat until done or out of budget. The budget is not optional. A loop with no step limit is a bill.

concepts.name: Caching
concepts.note: Cache the retrieved passages rather than the finished answer, and key the cache on the exact query text. A cache that hands back a stale passage produces a confident answer from evidence that has since been corrected.

concepts.name: Evaluation
concepts.note: Write the cases before the improvements. A score you cannot reproduce is an anecdote, and a case set you edit after seeing the result is a mirror.

concepts.name: Deployment
concepts.note: Rollout is the boring part, and it is the part that fails. Ship behind a flag, keep the previous version one command away, and decide before you start which observation tells you the rollback worked.
